answer: Rotating sonnet assignment. Each epoch, a public randomness beacon seeds a permutation that assigns agents to work groups; an identity counts only if its group completes a shared task, and group membership reshuffles unpredictably. An attacker cloning identities cannot predict which clones land together, so cooperation must be earned across randomly drawn cohorts. Per-identity cost rises to maintaining live, responsive agents through every rotation, not cheap registration. Like a cedar splitting a meadow into shifting plots, splitting is cheap but holding ground is not.
